title: One Place That Says Stop: A Supervisor That Combines Every Monitor, Latches, Keeps Every Cause, and Never Gets Less Strict When a Fault Is Added

questions.question: What should a field of Inputs that nobody filled in mean?
options: The safe case: an Inputs of all defaults gave normal
Nothing: defaults are skipped
A warning: defaults gave degraded and a cap of 0.5
The unsafe case: an Inputs of all defaults gave stopped, a cap of 0 and all six causes
questions.explanation: Every default is the dangerous reading, so a field somebody forgot to fill stops the robot instead of letting it go.

questions.question: A tilt warning (0.5 m/s) and a power share of 0.2 (0.4 m/s) are both present. What is the cap?
options: 0.5, the tilt's cap, since tilt outranks power
0.9, the two added
0.2, the power share itself
0.4: the lowest cap wins, and both reasons are reported
questions.explanation: The top speed of 2 m/s times a share of 0.2 is 0.4, lower than the tilt warning's 0.5. Both reasons are kept in the report.

questions.question: A robot stopped for a tilt loses its link as well, and both then go away. What is the state?
options: normal: nothing is wrong any more
Still stopped, with both causes on record, until a reset: refused while a cause remains
degraded, until the operator confirms
Stopped, with only the tilt on record, since it came first
questions.explanation: Causes going away does not restart the robot. A reset is refused while any remains, and every cause seen since the latch is kept.

questions.question: Why keep every cause seen since the latch and not only the first?
options: The log is easier to read with more entries
Only the last cause matters, and it might be missed
The first is not always the one that matters, and a reset after one cause with another still there starts the robot towards a hazard the operator was not told of
So that the supervisor can count faults
questions.explanation: A robot that lost its link while tilting has two things to be looked at. Recording only the first would hide the second from the person who resets it.

questions.question: What was checked over all 1024 combinations of ten conditions?
options: That each combination had a test written for it
That the supervisor ran in under a millisecond
That a stop cause always stopped, and that adding a fault never made the mode or the cap less strict: 0 violations in 10240 additions
That at least one combination was normal
questions.explanation: 1008 combinations stopped, 15 were degraded and 1 was normal. Checking the property over all of them catches a rule that would have passed any single test.

questions.question: What is the supervisor's job compared with the stop path of lesson 19-02?
options: The supervisor decides; the stop path and the hardware enforce, and must work even if the process with the supervisor dies
The supervisor replaces the stop path
They are two names for the same code
The stop path decides and the supervisor enforces
questions.explanation: The supervisor gathers every monitor into one decision. The stop path and the hardware carry it out, and still stop the robot if the supervisor's process is gone.
